name: Adobe
description: In October 2013, 153 million Adobe accounts were breached. The data included internal IDs, usernames, emails, encrypted passwords and password hints in plain text.

name: LinkedIn
description: In May 2012, LinkedIn had 164 million email addresses and passwords exposed. Originally 6.5 million accounts, it was later revealed the full dataset was 164 million.

name: MySpace
description: In approximately 2008, MySpace suffered a data breach that exposed almost 360 million accounts containing email addresses and passwords stored as SHA-1 hashes.

name: Twitter
description: In early 2023, over 200 million Twitter records were spread on hacking forums. The data was obtained by exploiting a vulnerability in the Twitter API.

name: Facebook
description: In April 2019, a large dataset of Facebook records was found exposed on Amazon cloud servers. 533 million records including phone numbers, names, and email addresses.

name: Yahoo
description: In 2016, Yahoo announced that 3 billion of their user accounts had been breached in 2013, making it the largest known breach in history.

name: Dropbox
description: In mid-2012, Dropbox suffered a data breach which exposed the stored credentials of tens of millions of their customers.

name: Adobe Creative Cloud
description: In October 2019, Adobe's Creative Cloud service exposed user data including email addresses, account membership information, and payment status.

name: Canva
description: In May 2019, the graphic design tool website Canva suffered a data breach that impacted 137 million users.

name: eBay
description: In May 2014, eBay announced a cyberattack that occurred between late February and early March 2014. The breach exposed a database with 145 million records.

name: Equifax
description: In 2017, Equifax announced a breach exposing the personal data of 147.9 million Americans including Social Security numbers, birth dates, and addresses.

name: Target
description: In late 2013, Target suffered one of the largest retail breaches in history affecting 70 million customers and 40 million credit/debit card accounts.

name: Uber
description: In October 2016, Uber suffered a data breach affecting 57 million riders and drivers. Uber paid hackers $100,000 to delete the data and conceal the breach.

name: JP Morgan Chase
description: In 2014, JPMorgan Chase suffered a massive data breach that compromised data associated with over 83 million accounts, including 76 million households.

name: Anthem
description: In February 2015, health insurance company Anthem disclosed a breach of nearly 78.8 million records including SSNs, names, birth dates, addresses, and employment info.

name: Home Depot
description: In 2014, Home Depot had 56 million customer payment cards compromised using custom-built malware deployed on self-checkout systems.

name: Marriott International
description: In November 2018, Marriott announced a breach of the Starwood guest reservation database containing up to 500 million guest records dating back to 2014.

name: Capital One
description: In July 2019, Capital One announced a data breach affecting over 100 million individuals in the US and Canada, including SSNs, bank account numbers, and credit scores.

name: T-Mobile
description: In August 2021, T-Mobile disclosed a breach exposing personal data of 76.6 million people including SSNs, driver license info, and IMEI numbers.

name: T-Mobile 2023
description: In early 2023, T-Mobile disclosed another breach affecting 37 million customers via their API, exposing names, billing addresses, phone numbers, and emails.

name: Twitch
description: In October 2021, Twitch suffered a data breach exposing 125GB of data including streamer payout information, source code, and internal tools.

name: Nvidia
description: In February 2022, Nvidia was breached by the LAPSUS$ group, exposing employee credentials and proprietary data including source code.

name: Okta
description: In March 2022, authentication company Okta was breached via a third-party support provider, with access gained to customer tenant systems.

name: Samsung
description: In March 2022, Samsung was breached by LAPSUS$, exposing 190GB of data including source code for Galaxy devices and biometric authentication algorithms.

name: Revolut
description: In September 2022, fintech company Revolut suffered a social engineering attack that exposed personal data of 50,150 customers.

name: Lastpass
description: In December 2022, LastPass disclosed that hackers had stolen encrypted password vaults and unencrypted customer data in an attack first detected in August 2022.

name: Twitter 200M
description: In January 2023, an alleged database of 200 million Twitter user records was distributed on hacking forums for free, scraped via a vulnerability in 2021.

name: Thingiverse
description: In October 2020, the 3D printing community Thingiverse had a backup file containing 228 million unique email addresses exposed online.

name: Wattpad
description: In June 2020, the storytelling website Wattpad suffered a massive data breach exposing 271 million records with names, usernames, emails, and bcrypt passwords.

name: Wishbone
description: In May 2020, the Wishbone app had 40 million user records posted online including names, usernames, phone numbers, and emails.

name: Tokopedia
description: In May 2020, Indonesian e-commerce giant Tokopedia suffered a breach with 91 million records exposed including usernames, emails and hashed passwords.

name: Zoom
description: In April 2020, as Zoom usage surged during COVID-19, over 500,000 Zoom accounts were found for sale on dark web forums with email/password combinations.

name: EasyJet
description: In May 2020, EasyJet disclosed a data breach affecting 9 million customers, with 2,208 customers having their credit card details accessed.

name: Microsoft
description: In January 2020, Microsoft disclosed a breach of customer support records spanning 14 years. 250 million records with email addresses and support details were exposed.

name: Clubhouse
description: In April 2021, data from 3.8 million Clubhouse users was posted on a hacker forum. The data was scraped from the app's public API.

name: Twitch Chat Logs
description: In May 2022, a large dataset of Twitch chat logs dating back to 2009 was released containing 181 million lines of chat messages.

name: Gravatar
description: In October 2020, 114 million Gravatar profiles were scraped from their public API. The data contained email hashes and profile information.

name: Ledger
description: In July 2020, hardware crypto wallet company Ledger had their e-commerce database breached, exposing over 1 million customer email addresses and 272,000 physical addresses.

name: Chegg
description: In September 2018, education technology company Chegg had 40 million user records exposed including names, emails, shipping addresses and passwords.

name: Quora
description: In December 2018, Q&A platform Quora disclosed a breach affecting 100 million users, with names, emails, encrypted passwords, and data from linked networks exposed.

name: 500px
description: In July 2018, photography website 500px suffered a data breach affecting nearly 15 million users. The exposed data included names, usernames, emails, and hashed passwords.

name: Houzz
description: In late 2018, home renovation website Houzz disclosed a data breach affecting an undisclosed number of users. 48 million records were later found circulating.

name: MyFitnessPal
description: In February 2018, diet app MyFitnessPal (owned by Under Armour) was breached. 144 million unique email addresses, usernames, and hashed passwords were exposed.

name: Dailymotion
description: In October 2016, video platform Dailymotion suffered a data breach that impacted over 85 million accounts with email addresses and hashed passwords.

name: Dubsmash
description: In December 2018, video messaging service Dubsmash had 162 million user records exposed including emails, usernames, and salted SHA-256 passwords.

name: Armor Games
description: In early 2019, online gaming platform Armor Games suffered a data breach exposing 11 million user records including emails, usernames, and passwords.

name: CafePress
description: In February 2019, custom merchandise platform CafePress was breached exposing 23 million records including emails, names, passwords, and physical addresses.

name: Chegg 2
description: In April 2019, Chegg was breached again. 700,000 records belonging to the Thinkful subsidiary were exposed with names, emails, and passwords.

name: DoorDash
description: In May 2019, DoorDash suffered a data breach affecting 4.9 million users, merchants and drivers exposing names, emails, delivery addresses, and partial credit card info.

name: Evite
description: In April 2019, online invitation service Evite disclosed a breach affecting 100 million accounts with names, emails, usernames, passwords, and phone numbers.

name: GameSpy
description: In 2004, GameSpy suffered a breach exposing 3 million user records with usernames, email addresses, and MD5 hashed passwords.

name: iMesh
description: In September 2013, peer-to-peer file sharing service iMesh was breached, exposing almost 50 million user accounts with email addresses and salted MD5 passwords.

name: Kickstarter
description: In February 2014, crowdfunding platform Kickstarter was breached. 5.2 million user records were exposed with usernames, emails, and salted SHA-1 passwords.

name: Last.fm
description: In March 2012, music streaming service Last.fm was breached exposing 43 million user records with email addresses and unsalted MD5 passwords.

name: LiveJournal
description: In 2014, blogging platform LiveJournal was breached exposing 26 million user records. The data contained usernames, email addresses, and MD5 passwords.

name: Netlog
description: In November 2012, Belgian social network Netlog was breached. 49 million records were exposed with email addresses and SHA-1 password hashes.

name: Ning
description: In 2012, social networking platform Ning suffered a data breach exposing 40 million user records with email addresses and salted SHA-1 passwords.

name: Pemiblanc
description: In April 2018, credential stuffing list 'Pemiblanc' containing 30 million unique email addresses and passwords obtained from various other breaches appeared online.

name: RockYou
description: In December 2009, social application website RockYou was breached exposing 32 million user accounts stored in plain text, which became one of the most referenced password lists.

name: Snapchat
description: In January 2014, 4.6 million Snapchat usernames and partially obscured phone numbers were published online after the company failed to patch a known vulnerability.

name: VK
description: In 2012, Russian social network VK was breached. 93 million user records were exposed with email addresses, phone numbers, plain text passwords, and names.

name: Zoosk
description: In 2011, online dating site Zoosk suffered a breach of 52 million user records with email addresses and hashed passwords.

name: Exactis
description: In June 2018, marketing firm Exactis had a database of 340 million records exposed. The data contained highly detailed personal profiles on virtually every US citizen.

name: Verifications.io
description: In February 2019, email validation service Verifications.io exposed 763 million unique email addresses alongside names, phone numbers, and other personal data.

name: Collection #1
description: In January 2019, a massive collection of credentials known as Collection #1 was published, containing 773 million unique email addresses and 21 million unique passwords aggregated from thousands of breaches.

name: Zynga
description: In September 2019, game developer Zynga (Words With Friends) was breached. 173 million player records were exposed with emails, usernames, phone numbers, and hashed passwords.

name: Spotify
description: In November 2020, Spotify had 350,000 accounts accessed via credential stuffing, with private playlists, email addresses, and listening history exposed.

name: Deezer
description: In November 2022, music streaming service Deezer had 257 million user records stolen from a third-party contractor. Names, emails, dates of birth, and genders were exposed.

name: Twilio
description: In August 2022, communications platform Twilio was compromised via a phishing attack on employees, affecting 125 customer organizations and ~1,900 Authy users.

name: Neopets
description: In July 2022, Neopets was breached with 69 million user accounts and 460MB of source code exposed. Usernames, emails, IP addresses, and personal details were included.

name: Shields Health Care Group
description: In June 2022, health care company Shields suffered a breach affecting 2 million patients, exposing SSNs, insurance details, medical records, and financial information.

name: Plex
description: In August 2022, media streaming platform Plex suffered a breach exposing usernames, email addresses, and encrypted passwords for 15 million users.

name: Slick Wraps
description: In February 2020, phone skin company Slick Wraps suffered a breach after a researcher discovered an unsecured S3 bucket. 370,000 customer records were exposed.

name: Wishbone 2020
description: In March 2020, Wishbone's entire database of 40 million records was posted online for free, including emails, phone numbers, usernames, and plain text passwords.

name: Aptoide
description: In April 2020, Android app marketplace Aptoide had 20 million user records leaked by hackers including email addresses, hashed passwords, and IP addresses.

name: Mathway
description: In April 2020, math problem solver website Mathway had 25 million user records exposed including email addresses and hashed passwords.

name: HomeChef
description: In May 2020, meal kit delivery service HomeChef suffered a breach affecting 8 million customers. Names, emails, phone numbers, and hashed passwords were exposed.

name: BigBasket
description: In October 2020, Indian grocery delivery service BigBasket suffered a breach affecting 20 million customers. Email addresses, hashed passwords, and addresses were exposed.

name: Pixlr
description: In January 2021, online photo editor Pixlr had 1.9 million user records exposed including email addresses, usernames, countries, and hashed passwords.

name: MeetMindful
description: In January 2021, dating site MeetMindful suffered a breach with 2.28 million user records posted online including names, emails, Facebook tokens, and location data.

name: Clubillion
description: In March 2020, casino app Clubillion exposed a database containing daily logs of 200 million users with IP addresses, winnings, and email addresses.

name: FlexBooker
description: In December 2021, appointment scheduling service FlexBooker was hit by a cyberattack. 3.7 million records with email addresses, phone numbers, and hashed passwords were stolen.

name: SuperVPN, GeckoVPN, ChatVPN
description: In May 2021, data from 21 million users of SuperVPN, GeckoVPN, and ChatVPN was posted online including emails, usernames, countries, and device information.

name: Raychat
description: In February 2021, Iranian messaging app Raychat had its entire database of 267 million accounts wiped by a bot, with 150 million records leaked including private messages.

name: Experian
description: In August 2020, credit bureau Experian South Africa suffered a breach affecting 24 million South Africans and 793,749 businesses.

name: Animal Jam
description: In October 2020, children's online game Animal Jam was breached. 46 million records were exposed including parent email addresses and encrypted passwords.

name: Cash App
description: In December 2022, Block Inc. (formerly Square) confirmed that a former Cash App employee had downloaded reports containing customer data including names, brokerage account numbers, and portfolio values.

name: DraftKings
description: In November 2022, sports betting platform DraftKings disclosed a credential stuffing attack affecting 68,000 customers with financial losses reported.

name: Twitter 2021 API
description: In 2021, a vulnerability in the Twitter API allowed email/phone number enumeration. A dataset of 5.4 million profiles was later shared on a hacking forum in 2022.

name: Cleartrip
description: In July 2022, Indian travel booking platform Cleartrip suffered a breach with internal data including customer records claimed to have been stolen.

name: Shields Health
description: In March 2022, medical imaging company Shields Health Care Group was breached, exposing PHI of 2 million patients including SSNs and diagnosis codes.

name: OpenSea
description: In June 2022, NFT marketplace OpenSea had an email list of 1.8 million users exfiltrated by a malicious employee of their email delivery vendor Customer.io.

name: Weibo
description: In March 2019, Chinese social media giant Weibo had 504 million user records exposed. In 2020, a portion of this data was offered for sale online.

name: Ronin Network
description: In March 2022, Axie Infinity's Ronin Network was hacked for $625 million in cryptocurrency. User wallet addresses and transaction histories were exposed.

name: AT&T
description: In August 2021, data claiming to be from AT&T containing 70 million records appeared online including SSNs, dates of birth, and encrypted account PINs.

name: AT&T 2024
description: In March 2024, AT&T confirmed that data from 73 million current and former customers was released on the dark web, including SSNs and account passcodes.

name: 23andMe
description: In October 2023, genetic testing company 23andMe disclosed a credential stuffing attack that ultimately exposed the data of 6.9 million users via the DNA Relatives feature.

name: Duolingo
description: In January 2023, language learning app Duolingo had 2.6 million user records scraped via their public API and posted on a hacking forum.

name: PeopleConnect
description: In January 2023, background check company PeopleConnect (Intelius, TruthFinder) was breached. 20 million rows of customer data including names, emails, and phone numbers were exposed.

name: Zacks Investment Research
description: In 2022, financial research firm Zacks Investment Research suffered a breach of 8.9 million records including names, addresses, phone numbers, and passwords.

name: Shields Health Care 2
description: In May 2024, Shields Health Care disclosed a second breach affecting 2.3 million patients with PHI exposed.

name: Ticketmaster
description: In May 2024, Live Nation/Ticketmaster confirmed a data breach affecting 560 million customers. The data was claimed by ShinyHunters and included names, addresses, phone numbers, and partial payment card information.

name: Snowflake / Santander
description: In May 2024, Santander Bank disclosed a breach via a third-party provider (Snowflake) affecting 30 million customers in Chile, Spain, and Uruguay.

name: Change Healthcare
description: In February 2024, Change Healthcare (UnitedHealth Group) was hit by the ALPHV/BlackCat ransomware group, impacting 100 million+ patients with medical and financial data stolen.

name: National Public Data
description: In August 2024, background check company National Public Data confirmed a breach of 2.9 billion records scraped from public sources containing SSNs, addresses, names, and relatives.

name: Dell
description: In May 2024, Dell notified customers of a breach involving 49 million customer records including names, physical addresses, Dell hardware, and order information.

name: MOVEit
description: In May 2023, a zero-day vulnerability in MOVEit Transfer was exploited by the Cl0p ransomware group, affecting hundreds of organizations and over 95 million individuals.

name: GoAnywhere MFT
description: In January 2023, Fortra's GoAnywhere MFT file transfer software was exploited by Cl0p, affecting 130+ organizations and millions of individuals.

name: Reddit
description: In June 2018, Reddit was breached via SMS 2FA bypass. An attacker accessed backup data from 2007, exposing usernames, salted hashed passwords, and emails.

name: Discord
description: In May 2023, Discord disclosed that a third-party support agent's account was compromised, exposing 760,000 user records with email addresses and support ticket content.

name: Activision
description: In February 2023, Activision confirmed a December 2022 phishing breach exposing employee data and game release schedules.

name: Shields 2023
description: In September 2023, data broker Gravy Analytics' parent company suffered a breach exposing 3.5 million location data records.

name: Pizza Hut Australia
description: In September 2023, Pizza Hut Australia disclosed a breach affecting 193,000 customers including names, delivery addresses, and order history.

name: Mortgage Loan Data
description: In October 2023, mortgage servicing company Mr. Cooper suffered a breach affecting 14.7 million customers with names, addresses, SSNs, and financial information exposed.
